<h1 id="Priestley-Taylor-(1972)-Radiation-Based-ET%E2%82%80">Priestley-Taylor (1972) Radiation-Based ET₀<a class="anchor-link" href="#Priestley-Taylor-(1972)-Radiation-Based-ET%E2%82%80">¶</a></h1><p><strong>Citation:</strong> Priestley CHB, Taylor RJ (1972). <em>Monthly Weather Review</em> 100(2): 81-92.</p>
<p><strong>Abstract.</strong> Priestley–Taylor estimates reference evapotranspiration from available energy and temperature-dependent thermodynamic factors, using α = 1.26 for well-watered surfaces. This notebook implements the radiation pathway, cross-checks analytical cases and FAO-56 Example 18 (Uccle) against <code>benchmark_priestley_taylor.json</code>, and visualizes gradients and sensitivities used in ET₀ intercomparisons.</p>
<p><strong>For other springs:</strong> Primal capability <code>science.et0_priestley_taylor</code>; Rust binary <code>validate_priestley_taylor</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Theory">Theory<a class="anchor-link" href="#Theory">¶</a></h2><p>$$\mathrm{ET}_{0,\mathrm{PT}} = \alpha \,\frac{\Delta}{\Delta + \gamma}\,\frac{R_n - G}{\lambda},\quad \alpha = 1.26$$</p>
<p>Reference implementation (FAO-style mm day⁻¹ conversion):</p>
<p>$$\mathrm{ET}_{0,\mathrm{PT}} = \max\left(0,\;\alpha \cdot 0.408 \cdot \frac{\Delta}{\Delta + \gamma}\cdot (R_n - G)\right)$$</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
